rule: In chart/values.yaml, describe auto-generated config values as 'generated by default from .Values.<helmPath>' and recommend configuring via the Helm value rather than overriding config.* directly.
trigger: A values.yaml comment says a config key is 'deprecated' or 'only possible' via a direct override when it is actually auto-generated from a Helm value path.
rationale: config.* entries are rendered into airflow.cfg and can still be overridden directly by users; wording that says override is forbidden or deprecated misleads users about the actual precedence mechanism.

evidence.excerpt: describe it as generated by default and recommend using dagProcessor.dagBundleConfigList

rule: When a Helm config flag's behaviour depends on another flag (e.g. statsd_on gated on otelCollector.metricsEnabled), document the dependency in both values.yaml and values.schema.json.
trigger: A ternary or conditional expression in config: block of values.yaml references two or more .Values fields but only one field has an explanatory comment.
rationale: values.schema.json is the source for generated Helm chart documentation; omitting the dependency there means users reading the docs see an incomplete picture of when the flag is active.

evidence.excerpt: add this information next to statsd.enabled in values.yaml and values.schema.json

rule: Do not include implementation-detail comments in chart/values.yaml; keep comments at the user-facing configuration level only.
trigger: A values.yaml comment explains internal template guard logic, schema validation mechanics, or Helm helper function internals rather than describing what the field controls.
rationale: values.yaml is a configuration surface for end users; internal implementation details are noise at that level and should live in template files or developer docs instead.

evidence.excerpt: Implementation details that are rather not needed on configuration level.

rule: Release-tooling shell scripts in dev/ must branch on $(uname) to handle both macOS (BSD date) and Linux (GNU date) syntax.
trigger: A shell script in dev/ uses date --utc (GNU-only) or date -v (BSD-only) without an OS check.
rationale: Airflow maintainers run release scripts on both macOS and Linux; a single-platform date invocation silently breaks the release workflow on the other OS.

evidence.excerpt: macOS (BSD date) … Linux (GNU date) … Unsupported OS exit 1

rule: Images used only by kustomize-overlay smoke tests must NOT be added to the static Breeze k8s image list; they are auto-discovered from the overlay manifest via _discover_overlay_images().
trigger: A new image entry is added to the static Breeze k8s preload list in kubernetes_commands.py for an image that appears only in chart/kustomize-overlays/.
rationale: breeze k8s smoke-test-overlay auto-discovers overlay images from the rendered manifest and preloads them automatically; adding them to the static list creates a second maintenance point that can diverge.

evidence.excerpt: overlay images must NOT be added here; auto-discovers them from the rendered manifest

rule: New path-parsing or git-worktree logic added to Breeze must be covered by unit tests for: an absolute gitdir path, a relative gitdir path, and the non-worktree case.
trigger: A function that reads .git file content or derives paths from AIRFLOW_ROOT_PATH is added to path_utils.py or shell_params.py without corresponding tests mocking those three scenarios.
rationale: .parent.parent derivations and gitdir parsing are easy to break silently; without explicit tests for relative paths and the non-worktree case, regressions go undetected.

evidence.excerpt: Would be good to add tests that mock AIRFLOW_ROOT_PATH / ".git" as a file

rule: Fragile path-derivation logic in Breeze (e.g. locating the main .git directory from a worktree gitdir) must be encapsulated in a single helper; do not duplicate it across docker_command_utils.py and shell_params.py.
trigger: The expression .parent.parent (or equivalent worktree-root derivation) appears in more than one file under dev/breeze/src/ when referring to the main git repository root.
rationale: The assumption that worktree gitdirs are always two levels deep from .git/ is fragile; duplicating it means a structural change must be tracked and fixed in multiple places.

evidence.excerpt: parent.parent path derivation to find the main .git directory is duplicated in two places

rule: get_git_worktree_root() must resolve a relative gitdir: path to an absolute path before returning, because Docker bind mounts require absolute paths.
trigger: Path(git_content.removeprefix("gitdir: ")) is returned directly without checking is_absolute() and resolving against AIRFLOW_ROOT_PATH.
rationale: The gitdir: pointer in a .git file can be relative; passing a relative path to Docker as a bind mount produces a confusing Docker error rather than a clear failure.

evidence.excerpt: Docker bind mounts require absolute paths, so a relative gitdir would produce an invalid mount

rule: When using prek in Breeze helper scripts or error messages, use --hook-stage (not --stage) to match prek's CLI flag name.
trigger: A prek invocation or instructional string in dev/breeze/ uses --stage instead of --hook-stage.
rationale: prek --help exposes --hook-stage; using --stage is incorrect and will confuse contributors trying to reproduce the suggested command.

evidence.excerpt: prek --help shows --stage and we generally use --hook-stage

rule: CacheStore entries in Breeze must wrap the stored payload under a dedicated key (e.g. {"profile": ...}) so that internal cache metadata (cached_at) is not leaked into the runtime object returned to callers.
trigger: A CacheStore.save() call stores a plain dict directly, and the corresponding CacheStore.get() return value is used as the runtime object without stripping cache metadata fields.
rationale: CacheStore injects a cached_at field when TTL is enabled; returning the raw store value gives callers a different object shape depending on whether data came from the API or disk, breaking consumers that expect a consistent schema.

evidence.excerpt: callers get a different shape depending on whether the profile came from the API or disk

rule: CI reproduction instructions generated by Breeze must use GITHUB_SHA to check out the exact commit, not FETCH_HEAD, so the instructions remain stable as the PR ref advances.
trigger: A ReproductionCommand in reproduce_ci.py emits git checkout FETCH_HEAD after a fetch of refs/pull/….
rationale: refs/pull/<n>/head moves when new commits are pushed; checking out FETCH_HEAD after re-fetching at a later time gives a different commit than the one that produced the failing CI run.

evidence.excerpt: FETCH_HEAD can drift over time because the ref can move as new commits are pushed

rule: When Breeze emits CLI flag pairs in reproduction commands, always select the long-form alias (param.opts[-1] / param.secondary_opts[-1]), not the first alias (param.opts[0]).
trigger: A flag-pair branch in build_reproduction_command_from_context() uses param.opts[0] or param.secondary_opts[0] to select the flag to emit.
rationale: param.opts[0] can be the short alias (e.g. -f); reproduction commands should be copy/paste friendly and use the long form (--force) consistently.

evidence.excerpt: pick the short alias when both are present, e.g. -f instead of --force

rule: The KUSTOMIZE_OVERLAYS_FILES file group in selective_checks.py must include chart/templates/ and chart/files/ because overlay smoke tests depend on Helm template changes.
trigger: A diff adds or modifies FileGroupForCi.KUSTOMIZE_OVERLAYS_FILES in selective_checks.py without including r"^chart/templates/" and r"^chart/files/" patterns.
rationale: Kustomize overlays render on top of the Helm chart templates; a template change can break an overlay test without triggering the overlay CI pipeline if templates/ is excluded from the file group.

evidence.excerpt: customisations and their content can depend on how templates are constructed and created

rule: Breeze utility functions must not mix human-readable error sentinel strings into list[str] collections of job names; use None, a result object, or a typed union to signal lookup failure.
trigger: A function with return type list[str] (or similar job-name collection) returns a string constant such as FAILED_JOBS_LOOKUP_ERROR on failure instead of None or raising an exception.
rationale: Downstream consumers of job-name lists treat every entry as a real job identifier; an error string produces false recovery paths or incorrect rendering and comparisons.

evidence.excerpt: mixes two different concepts (job names vs. lookup failure) and can confuse downstream consumers

rule: Tests for Breeze CLI flag-pair rendering must include a case with both a short alias and a long alias to assert the long form is emitted.
trigger: A test in dev/breeze/tests/ for build_reproduction_command_from_context or similar flag-rendering logic only tests flags that have a single (long) form, omitting the short+long alias scenario.
rationale: Without a test covering short+long alias pairs, regressions that accidentally emit the short form (e.g. -f instead of --force) will go undetected.

evidence.excerpt: no test asserting that flag pairs with both short and long aliases render using the preferred long form
